question: Which of the following is the longest range in the lesser Himalayas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pir Panjal Range**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pir Panjal Range is the longest range in the Lesser Himalayas: 
 
• Location: The Pir Panjal Range runs through the states of Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. 
 
• Elevation: The average elevation of the range is 5,000 meters above sea level. 
 
• Notable features: The range includes the Jawahar tunnel, Atal tunnel, and Banihal tunnel.
 
• The Banihal Railway Tunnel is India's longest railway tunnel.
 
• The range also includes the peaks of Deo Tibba and Indrasan. 
 
• Rivers: The Jhelum, Kishanganga, and Chenab rivers flow through the range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Zanskar Range, Ladakh Range, and Karakoram Range are all mountain ranges in the Ladakh region of India.
 
• The Zanskar Range is located south of the Ladakh Range, which is in turn located south of the Karakoram Range. 
 
• Karakoram Range
 
• Part of a complex of mountain ranges that also includes the Hindu Kush, Himalaya, and Pamir ranges.
 
• The Karakoram Range has eight mountains with peaks over 7,500 meters (24,600 ft) high, and four of those are higher than 8,000 meters (26,000 ft). 
 
• Ladakh
 
• A cold desert in the northernmost part of India, Ladakh is home to some of the world's highest mountain peaks.
 
• Many of these peaks are unclimbed and unnamed due to security reasons. 
 
• Zanskar Range
 
• One of the main ranges in Ladakh, along with the Ladakh Range, Kailas, and Karakoram
